body:
# Independent audit: captured-side BM equality does not glue globally


`candidate 60dfb1dd651b7ddd`.
Result: **PASS**. The counterexample satisfies every stated proper-cut,
interior-point, full positive-circuit, actual Minkowski-sum, and
captured-side equality condition. The missing whole-body BM equality
cannot be inferred from them. This audit additionally computes exact
ordinary halfspace depths at the specified point and shows that none
of the displayed caps is ordinary-critical there.

## 1. Whole bodies and actual Minkowski addition

In the source's cyclic order, the endpoint polygons are

    A: (-1,2), (-2,-1), (2,-3), (2,-1),
    B: (-13/8,17/8), (-5/2,-1/2), (3/2,-5/2), (3/2,-1).

Direct intersections of the four stated support lines recover these
vertices. Every corresponding support inequality has a positive
right side, so the origin is strictly inside both polygons.

The average support inequalities contain `(A+B)/2`. Their polygon
has vertices

    K: (-21/16,33/16), (-9/4,-3/4), (7/4,-11/4), (7/4,-1).

Each is the average of the correspondingly indexed A and B vertices.
Thus all K vertices belong to `(A+B)/2`, proving the reverse
containment and the exact set identity `K=(A+B)/2`. The origin also
strictly satisfies all four inequalities of K.

Shoelace integration gives

    |A|=10,       |B|=271/32,       |K|=1183/128.

The exact excess over the squared BM root average is

    |K|-[(sqrt(|A|)+sqrt(|B|))/2]^2
      =(37-sqrt(1355))/8
      =7/[4(37+sqrt(1355))] > 0.                    (1)

The positivity follows from `37^2-1355=14`, not a decimal comparison.
This is consistent with the source's equivalent squared certificate
`(4|K|-|A|-|B|)^2-4|A||B|=7/2`.

The two bodies cannot be positively homothetic. Their uniquely
oriented lower sloping edges both have vector `(4,-2)`, requiring
homothety ratio one; their uniquely oriented right vertical edges
have vectors `(0,2)` and `(0,3/2)`, requiring ratio 3/4. A negative
homothety is impossible as well: it would send the only right
vertical edge of A to a left vertical edge, which B does not have.

## 2. All actual cap polygons and homotheties

The halfspaces are

    H_1={x>=0},       H_2={y>=0},       H_3={x+y<=0}.

Their normals form a minimal rank-two positive circuit. They cover
the whole plane and all boundaries are included. Exact clipping gives
the following cyclic cap vertices, with cyclic starting point
irrelevant:

    A_1: (0,-2), (2,-3), (2,-1), (0,1),
    B_1: (0,-7/4), (3/2,-5/2), (3/2,-1), (0,1/2),
    K_1: (0,-15/8), (7/4,-11/4), (7/4,-1), (0,3/4).

    A_2: (-5/3,0), (1,0), (-1,2),
    B_2: (-7/3,0), (1/2,0), (-13/8,17/8),
    K_2: (-2,0), (3/4,0), (-21/16,33/16).

    A_3: (-2,-1), (2,-3), (2,-2), (-5/4,5/4),
    B_3: (-5/2,-1/2), (3/2,-5/2), (3/2,-3/2), (-7/4,7/4),
    K_3: (-9/4,-3/4), (7/4,-11/4), (7/4,-7/4), (-3/2,3/2).

Applying the three proposed maps to every A cap vertex gives exactly
the corresponding B cap vertices:

    T_1(x)=(3/4)x+(0,-1/4),
    T_2(x)=(17/16)x+(-9/16,0),
    T_3(x)=x+(-1/2,1/2).

The translations are tangent to their respective actual cut lines.
The averaged maps `(Id+T_i)/2` give exactly the displayed K cap
vertices. Convexity therefore proves each actual set identity

    K intersect H_i=((A intersect H_i)+(B intersect H_i))/2.

The source's captured-side area table checks:

    i       |A_i|       |B_i|       |K_i|
    1         5         45/16      245/64
    2        8/3        289/96     363/128
    3       55/8        55/8       55/8.

All areas are positive and smaller than their corresponding full
area. Hence all six endpoint cuts are proper, and their boundaries
meet the bodies without any empty/tangent substitution. Since the
homothety ratios are positive, the cap identities give the exact
root equalities in the question. All three normalized endpoint
fraction pairs are unequal, exactly as stated in the source.

## 3. A finite exact certificate for ordinary depth at an interior origin

Here is the elementary candidate principle used for the extra depth
calculation. Let P be a convex polygon containing the origin in its
interior, and let rho(theta)>0 be its continuous radial function.
The area of the halfplane sector between angles theta and theta+pi is

    F(theta)=(1/2) integral_theta^(theta+pi) rho(t)^2 dt.

It is continuously differentiable, with

    F'(theta)=[rho(theta+pi)^2-rho(theta)^2]/2.       (2)

Thus at a minimizing direction the two opposite boundary points of
the chord through zero have equal distance from zero. Write them as
p and -p. They lie on an edge of P and the reflected image of another
edge of P. One can therefore find every isolated stationary chord by
intersecting the finitely many original edges with reflected edges.

If two relevant edge segments overlap on one line, (2) vanishes on
the corresponding angular interval and the cap area is constant
there. An endpoint of that interval is a direction through a polygon
vertex, so including all vertex directions covers that case too.
This proves a finite exact candidate method: use the vertex
directions and all original-edge/reflected-edge intersection
directions, checking both sides of each line. No generic-position
or smoothness assumption is needed.

For A, B, and K, solving the sixteen original/reflected edge-pair
systems produces respectively just the following two intersection
points:

    A: +/-(-3/2,1/2),
    B: +/-(-3/2,2),
    K: +/-(-27/16,15/16).

There are no coincident edge segments in these polygons. The smaller
cap areas along the four vertex directions, in the cyclic orders
displayed in Section 1, are

    A: 25/6,      10/3,    34/9,     18/7;
    B: 625/416,   343/96,  27/16,    625/352;
    K: 343/128,   225/64,  343/128,  7203/3200.

These numbers follow by intersecting a line through the origin and
the listed vertex with the opposite polygon edge, followed by a
triangle or polygon area calculation. The new stationary-chord
directions have smaller-side areas respectively

    5/2,       3/2,       9/4.

Each is smaller than every corresponding entry of the preceding
row. The closest comparisons are exact:
`625/416-3/2=1/416` and `7203/3200-9/4=3/3200`.
The finite candidate principle proves the exact raw ordinary depths
at the origin:

    depth_A(0) in area units = 5/2,
    depth_B(0) in area units = 3/2,
    depth_K(0) in area units = 9/4.                  (3)

Minimizing containing halfspaces are respectively

    {x+3y>=0},       {4x+3y>=0},       {5x+9y>=0}.

Any containing halfspace can be moved inward to a through-origin
one without increasing its area, so the calculation indeed covers
all containing halfspaces, not only those initially parameterized
in (2). All boundaries carry zero area. Dividing (3) by full areas
gives normalized depths

    1/4,       48/271,       288/1183.               (4)

In particular every one of the three originally displayed caps has
strictly MORE area than the depth at zero in each corresponding
body. None is ordinary-critical at that point. Also every value in
(4) is less than 4/9, so ordinary Grünbaum at each body's own
centroid guarantees that zero is not an ordinary deepest point in
any of the three bodies. This limits what stronger critical-cap
statements the example can refute.

## 4. Actual integer-fiber embedding and scope

The convex hull of the two endpoint fibers at -1 and 1 has exactly
A,K,B at integer bases -1,0,1, since K is their actual Minkowski
midpoint. Its total mixed area is

    10+271/32+1183/128=3547/128.

The largest fiber is A, of area 10, which is strictly less than
half this total. The three ambient caps parallel to the integer
axis have masses

    745/64,       3269/384,       165/8,

respectively. They are unequal, so they cannot all be globally
critical caps at one mixed point. The source makes no such claim.

The counterexample conclusively refutes global homothety from the
specified simultaneous captured-side equalities and proper
through-point circuit alone. It does not refute an additional
hypothesis of whole-body BM equality or a stronger requirement
involving genuinely critical caps. No OC conclusion follows.

The independent verifier is
`supporting computation verify_cap_gluing_counterexample_and_origin_depths.py`. It uses
exact rational polygon operations and enumerates the proved finite
stationary-chord candidates. It originally passed 105 exact checks; with the later roof-lift checks, the same verifier passes 154 exact checks. The argument above explains why that
finite list certifies the continuous infimum.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
